messages:
morgan: heads up — short ~2min burst of 502s at 13:04 PDT impacting customer_id=amethyst. Can someone point me to the fastest dashboards/queries to grab traces + logs? Also thinking we might need a quick alert tweak so SREs don't page on transient blips.

ashley: do you have a sample x-request-id from one of the 502s? makes grabbing the trace trivial.

morgan: yes: x-request-id=req-0a1b2c (came from the customer report). saw ~25 errors in a 90s window.

ashley: quick places: Grafana ingress errors dash -> https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/ingress/errors (filter var=customer: amethyst). Kibana logs: https://kibana.redwood.ai/app/discover#/?_g=()&_a=(query:(language:kuery,query:'customer_id:\"amethyst\" AND status:502'))

eng-observability-bot: I can generate a short trace sample when you give me an x-request-id. Use `/trace req-0a1b2c` to fetch and attach.

raj: if you want a quick metric hit, run this in Prometheus (gives per-route 5xx rate):

```promql
sum by(route)(rate(http_requests_total{status=~\"5..\",env=\"prod\"}[1m]))
```

That'll show if the 502s are isolated to `ingress-proxy` or spread.

tara: on alerting: we should avoid paging for 1-2min microbursts. My quick suggestion: change the existing `High5xxRate` alert from `for: 5m` to `for: 10m` and add a minimum absolute count condition so tiny routes don't page. e.g.:

```yaml
expr: (increase(http_requests_total{status=~\"5..\",env=\"prod\"}[5m]) / increase(http_requests_total{env=\"prod\"}[5m])) > 0.02
and on() (increase(http_requests_total{env=\"prod\"}[5m]) > 20)
for: 10m
```

This requires >2% error rate AND >20 errors in the window, held for 10m. reduces noisy pages for low traffic routes.

ashley: +1 to that. For now, if you need immediate relief, we can add a temporary alert mute for the `amethyst` customer for 30m while we investigate — would you like me to do that?

morgan: yes please mute for 30m, and attach any traces you can get. we'll then decide whether to keep the tuning. thanks.

eng-observability-bot: mute applied for customer=amethyst for 30m :white_check_mark: (muted by ashley). Trace request queued for req-0a1b2c.

raj: one more triage tip — if the trace shows `upstream_connect_failed` at the proxy, it's likely backend capacity/TLS handshake. If it's `upstream_timeout`, check kvcache/agg-worker latencies.

tara: and remember to capture a span-level flamegraph if it recurs: `/debug/spans?request_id=req-0a1b2c` — handy to correlate to CPU/GPU spikes.

morgan: got the trace link from the bot, attaching to the customer ticket. will follow up here with root cause if/when we have it. thanks team :thumbsup:
